The Lagos State Government has suspended the movement of trucks into Magodo Estate for one week following a dispute between the Magodo Residents Association and the Shangisa Landlords Association over access to alternative land allocated to the landlords. The government also directed police personnel stationed at the estate’s entrance gate to remain there throughout the period to prevent a breakdown of law and order. Saturday PUNCH gathered that the decisions were reached at a stakeholders’ meeting convened by the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Lawal Pedro, SAN, on Thursday, following a disturbance at the entrance gate of Magodo Estate on Wednesday. According to a statement issued on Thursday by the Director of Public Affairs, Lagos State Ministry of Justice, Grace Alo, the meeting was attended by representatives of both associations, security agencies and relevant state government ministries and departments. The statement said the disturbance followed allegations that t20he judgment creditors, the Shangisa Landlords Association, had forcefully taken over the estate’s access gate in an attempt to gain entry to the alternative land allocated to them by the state government. The government said the one-week suspension of truck movement would allow it to explore a lasting solution to the access dispute. “Following extensive deliberations, all parties were urged to maintain peace, exercise restraint and refrain from any action capable of heightening tensions or undermining the ongoing efforts of the State Government to resolve the dispute,” the statement said. Magodo land dispute: Lagos suspends truck movement, orders suspects’ release Lagos cancels Saturday sanitation over INEC mock accreditation Lagos dismisses postponement rumours, says sanitation holds Saturday The government also directed the immediate release of any suspect still in detention in connection with the incident, although it acknowledged that some arrests had been made. It said another stakeholders’ meeting would be convened at the end of the one-week period to communicate its proposed solution to the parties. The dispute concerns access to alternative land allocated to the Shangisa landlords following the Supreme Court judgment in Suit No. SC/112/2002, Military Governor of Lagos State & 5 Ors. v. Adebayo Adeyiga & 7 Ors. The statement recalled that Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu approved the allocation to ensure compliance with the Supreme Court judgment and bring an end to the prolonged dispute surrounding its execution. According to the government, the allocation was intended to provide a lasting resolution to issues arising from the enforcement of the judgment. It urged residents and other stakeholders to remain calm, continue their lawful activities and cooperate with the authorities.
